sources.title: J. S. Milne, Fields and Galois Theory, v5.10
sources.locator: Chapter 3, printed p. 43, Lemma 3.25; Chapter 5, printed pp. 62-63, from the heading "Fundamental Theorem of Algebra" through Corollary 5.7

contents.name: Lemma 3.25, a quadratic extension in characteristic not 2 has the form F[sqrt(d)]
Theorem 5.6, the field C of complex numbers is algebraically closed
Corollary 5.7(a), the field C is the algebraic closure of R
Corollary 5.7(b), the set of all algebraic numbers is an algebraic closure of Q

sources.title: Keith Conrad, Applications of Galois Theory
sources.locator: Section 2, printed pp. 7-8, from the heading "Applications to Field Theory" through the end of Theorem 2.1

contents.name: Property (1), every odd degree polynomial in R[X] has a real root
Property (1), in particular no polynomial of odd degree greater than 1 in R[X] is irreducible
Property (2), every number in C has square roots in C
Property (4), a nontrivial finite p-group has a subgroup of index p
Theorem 2.1, the complex numbers are algebraically closed

sources.title: Keith Conrad, The Artin-Schreier Theorem
sources.locator: Section 3, printed pp. 1-4, Theorem 3.1 through Corollary 3.2

contents.name: Theorem 3.1 (Artin-Schreier), a field whose algebraic closure is a finite proper extension has quadratic algebraic closure and characteristic 0
contents.reason: The later-converse statement belongs with the real-closed and formally-real field block that frontier-20 does not build. The design records it as genuine later work rather than as material to pull forward into X-1.

contents.name: Corollary 3.2, if K is a subfield of R and [R:K] is finite then K=R
contents.reason: This is a field-ordering consequence of the full Artin-Schreier theorem, not a result needed by the Artin proof of the fundamental theorem of algebra or by its immediate algebraic consequences on this page.

canonical.name: Every odd-degree real polynomial has a real root
An irreducible real polynomial has degree 1 or an even degree
To prove the fundamental theorem of algebra, it suffices to split every real polynomial over C
A quadratic extension in characteristic not 2 is obtained by adjoining a square root
A field is algebraically closed exactly when every nonconstant polynomial splits, equivalently when it has no nontrivial finite extension
The complex numbers are algebraically closed
The complex numbers form an algebraic closure of R
The algebraic numbers in C form an algebraic closure of Q
A nonreal root of a real polynomial comes with its complex conjugate
An irreducible polynomial in R[x] has degree 1 or 2
Every real polynomial factors into linear and irreducible quadratic factors
A complex polynomial of degree n has exactly n roots counted with multiplicity
Artin-Schreier converse: a non-algebraically closed field with finite algebraic closure has quadratic algebraic closure and characteristic 0
canonical.reason: The design explicitly keeps this later field-theory converse for a real-closed/formally-real block rather than using X-1 to start that subject.
